panel.summary: `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'` silently changes the semantics of user queries, not just output formatting
panel.evidence: Line 144 sets the session TimeZone for every executeQuery. This is not purely a rendering concern: `now()`, `current_date`, `date_trunc('day', tstz_col)`, `tstz AT TIME ZONE ...` and any grouping/filtering on timestamptz now evaluate in UTC instead of the server's configured default timezone, so previously-correct user queries can return different rows/aggregates after this change. If only display formatting was intended, formatting the value (or setting only DateStyle) would avoid changing query results.
panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::`set timezone = 'utc'` silently changes the semantics of user queries, not just output formatting

coderabbit.summary: The `MONEY` assertion is locale-dependent and may fail on non-US clusters.
coderabbit.detail: **The `MONEY` assertion is locale-dependent and may fail on non-US clusters.** PostgreSQL formats the `money` type using the database's `lc_monetary` setting, which dictates the currency symbol and digit grouping. Since the test asserts the exact string `$1,234.56`, it will fail on databases configured with different locales. Either set `lc_monetary` to `en_US.UTF-8` in the test setup or avoid asserting the formatted string output.
coderabbit.finding_key: packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts::the `money` assertion is locale-dependent and may fail on non-us clusters.
